traditionalDress.men: A dhoti paired with a panjabi (the Bengali term for a kurta), often in cotton or silk with light embroidery around the collar; a shawl is added for cooler weather or formal occasions.
traditionalDress.women: The Tant saree (a crisp, lightweight cotton saree) for everyday wear, with the Garad saree (white with a red border) and richly patterned Baluchari or Kantha-embroidered silks reserved for festivals like Durga Puja.

festivals.name: Durga Puja
festivals.description: West Bengal's largest festival, a multi-day celebration of Goddess Durga's victory over evil, marked by elaborately themed pandals, artistic clay idols, and citywide festivities in Kolkata.

festivals.name: Poila Boishakh
festivals.description: The Bengali New Year, celebrated with new clothes, sweets, cultural programs, and the ceremonial opening of new account books (Haal Khata) by traders.

festivals.name: Ganga Mahotsav
festivals.description: A cultural festival held along the Ganges in Varanasi's Bengali community and in Bengal itself, showcasing music, dance, art, and boat races.

music: Rabindra Sangeet (songs composed by Rabindranath Tagore)
folklore: In the Sundarbans, Bonbibi is venerated by both Hindu and Muslim forest-dwellers as the guardian spirit of the mangrove forest. According to the legend, she defeated the demon tiger-king Dakshin Rai to protect a boy named Dukhe, and honey-collectors and woodcutters still invoke her protection before entering the forest.
